lead: Based on what you told me, your number one constraint is:
h1: Good months happen. Then they stop. [[And you don’t know why.]]
story: Last year, August was my best sales month, even though summer is usually slow. I thought it was luck. When we interviewed our customers, the pattern showed up: **Daniel Priestley had gone on the Diary of a CEO podcast**, and as a ScoreApp partner, his visibility was driving our enquiries. With a feedback loop built in, I could have sponsored his newsletter or pitched a content partnership, and {{doubled down on a good month.}}
fix_h: Collect data from every buyer, **and every non-buyer.**
fix_p: Every action a buyer or non-buyer takes across your customer journey feeds you data, so you can keep optimizing your sales assets. It’s all self-serve, which is why we’ve built a **14-point feedback loop** into it (more on that later). Even visitors who don’t buy leave you data, so month on month, it gets more profitable and you make more money from every visitor.
lens: Once you know your **Revenue Per Visitor™**, you stop guessing whether a month was a traffic, email or positioning problem, and start seeing it. The feedback loop runs across **all four quadrants** of the Compounding Revenue Per Visitor™ OS.
cta: Show me what’s driving my good and bad months
up_next: Next question: What have you already tried to improve your revenue?
